To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel RL approach to PAR, that is, we use a RL algorithm to learn good policies, we propose a family of off policy evaluation techniques to evaluate a solution, and that the RL approach outperforms the state-of-the-art myopic algorithms in terms of LTV.
we propose to use off-policy evaluation techniques to tackle two challenges in RL-based PAR systems: (i) how to compute a solution and (ii) how to ensure its safety before deployment.
RL algorithms equipped with off-policy evaluation techniques are better than the myopic techniques for PAR problems.

the problem of learning good personalized ad recommendation policies using RL techniques.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RL algorithm is more suitable than the myopic techniques for modern PAR systems.
the RL algorithm equipped with our proposed off-policy evaluation techniques outperformed all the myopic approaches in terms of LTV metric.
our proposed approach is a promising solution for PAR systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to use off-policy evaluation techniques to solve the two challenges of learning and evaluating an RL strategy for PAR.
, for the first time, we propose to apply RL algorithms to PAR problems, and show that the proposed framework is both theoretically and empirically better than the myopic techniques.
we provide a new approach for optimizing PAR systems, which can be used in conjunction with myopic techniques to improve their performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for PAR systems, it is important to use a LTV-based metric for evaluating the performance and optimizing the algorithm.
the RL approach can be successfully applied to PAR systems, and that off-policy evaluation techniques can be used to ensure the safety of the solution before deployment.
RL algorithms, if equipped with off-policy evaluation techniques, can be used to solve PAR problems in an online setting.
